name: Hagaba
title: Temple Servant Who Returned from Exile
summary: Hagaba was the ancestor of one of the families among the Nethinim (temple servants) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel. His descendants are mentioned in the lists of those who returned to rebuild the temple and restore worship in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned Among the Families of Temple Servants
keyEvents.description: Hagaba's descendants are listed among the Nethinim (temple servants) who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Listed in Nehemiah's Register
keyEvents.description: Hagaba's family is mentioned again in Nehemiah's register of those who returned from exile, confirming the family's role as temple servants.

keyEvents.title: Restoration of Temple Service
keyEvents.description: As part of the Nethinim, Hagaba's descendants helped restore temple service in Jerusalem after returning from the Babylonian exile.

keyEvents.title: The Role of the Nethinim in the Rebuilt Community
keyEvents.description: The temple servants, including the descendants of Hagab, were assigned homes and duties in rebuilt Jerusalem during Nehemiah's reforms.
